title: Epidemiology of ventriculostomy-related infections after stroke and traumatic brain injury: A Vizient Database Study (2019–2024)
content:
by Abhijit V. Lele, Lilac V. Langaroodi, Alyssa H. Harris, Hannah R. Murphy, Samuel N. Blacker

Background and Objectives

To examine the prevalence and factors associated with ventriculostomy-related infection (VRI) in adults with acute ischemic stroke (AIS), spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (s-ICH), and traumatic brain injury (TBI) across the United States.

Methods

In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed patients with ventriculostomy admitted to 340 hospitals in the Vizient® Clinical Data Base (June 2019–May 2024). VRI was identified via ICD-10 codes for meningitis/device-related infection. Multivariable logistic regression identified patient- and hospital-level factors associated with VRI; hospitals with VRI rates ≥5% were classified as high-VRI. We assessed temporal trends using Mann–Kendall tests, and sensitivity analyses used alternative length-of-stay and mortality models.

Results

Among 26,988 patients in the primary analytic cohort (Model 1: length of stay ≥5 days, survivors to discharge), VRI occurred in 1,526 (5.7%): 5.8% (AIS; 324/5,547), 6.3% (SAH; 414/6,522), 5.4% (s-ICH; 523/9,652), and 5.0% (TBI; 265/5,267). VRI odds decreased with age (45–64years aOR 0.82 [0.72–0.94]; 65–79years aOR 0.63 [0.51–0.78]; > 80years aOR 0.37 [0.26–0.53], vs 18–44years) and increased with Elixhauser comorbidity count (1: aOR 4.46 [1.58–18.66]; 2: aOR 5.55 [2.06–22.77]; ≥ 3: aOR 9.38 [3.54–38.13]), craniotomy/craniectomy (aOR 1.37 [1.00–1.83]), mechanical ventilation (aOR 1.24 [1.10–1.39]), and non-VRI healthcare-associated infection (aOR 1.41 [1.21–1.65]). VRI odds did not differ significantly by diagnosis. Of 340 hospitals, 134 (39.4%) had VRI rates ≥5%; these were associated with smaller bed capacity, higher ventriculostomy volume, and non-VRI HAI rates ≥5%. VRI rates rose significantly over time in the TBI cohort. Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings.

Discussion

VRI was found to affect nearly 6% of patients with acute brain injury, in this database study, requiring ventriculostomy. Hospital-level variation, comorbidity burden, and healthcare-associated infection rates were associated with VRI risk, highlighting targets for surveillance and prevention.
